:::{#cor-solution-unique}
#### Solvable for every right-hand side, and solvable uniquely

Let $\matr{A}$ be $m \times n$.

1. $\matr{A} \vecf{x} = \vecf{b}$ is consistent for every $\vecf{b} \in \reals^m$
   exactly when $\operatorname{rank}(\matr{A}) = m$.
2. A consistent system $\matr{A} \vecf{x} = \vecf{b}$ has exactly one solution
   exactly when $\operatorname{rank}(\matr{A}) = n$.

:::

::: proof

**Part 1.**
By @thm-consistency, the system is consistent for every $\vecf{b}$
exactly when $\mathcal{C}(\matr{A}) = \reals^m$.
$\mathcal{C}(\matr{A})$ is a subspace of $\reals^m$ (@thm-column-space-span) with dimension $\operatorname{rank}(\matr{A})$
(@thm-rank-dim), and $\dim(\reals^m) = m$ (@exm-dimension).
If the dimension is $m$, then $\mathcal{C}(\matr{A}) = \reals^m$ (@thm-subspace-equal-dim);
if $\mathcal{C}(\matr{A}) = \reals^m$, the dimension is $m$.

**Part 2.**
By @thm-solution-set, the solutions are a particular solution
plus the vectors of $\mathcal{N}(\matr{A})$,
so there is exactly one solution exactly when $\mathcal{N}(\matr{A}) = \cb{\vzero_n}$,
that is, when $\operatorname{nullity}(\matr{A}) = 0$
(a subspace of dimension $0$ has the empty list as a basis, whose span is $\cb{\vzero}$,
by @def-dimension and @def-span;
and $\cb{\vzero}$ has dimension $0$, by @exm-dimension).
By @thm-rank-nullity, that is when $\operatorname{rank}(\matr{A}) = n$.

:::

{{< slidebreak >}}

:::{#exm-solution-unique}
#### Three systems

- The $2 \times 3$ matrix $\begin{bmatrix} 1 & 0 & 1 \\ 0 & 1 & 1 \end{bmatrix}$ of @exm-rank-bound
  has rank $2 = m$, so every system with it is consistent,
  but $2 < 3 = n$, so the solutions are never unique.
- The $3 \times 2$ matrix $\mX = \begin{bmatrix} 1 & 1 \\ 1 & 2 \\ 1 & 3 \end{bmatrix}$ of @exm-gram-invertible
  has rank $2 = n$, so a consistent system has one solution,
  but $2 < 3 = m$, so some systems are inconsistent:
  $(1, 0, 0) \notin \mathcal{C}(\mX)$, because $a\,(1, 1, 1) + b\,(1, 2, 3)$
  has equal differences between consecutive entries,
  and $(1, 0, 0)$ does not.
- An invertible $p \times p$ matrix $\matr{A}$ has rank $p$:
  if $\matr{A} \vecf{x} = \vzero$ then

  $$
  \begin{aligned}
  \vecf{x} &= \matr{A}^{-1} \matr{A} \vecf{x} \\
  &= \vzero,
  \end{aligned}
  $$

  so its nullity is $0$ and its rank is $p$ (@thm-rank-nullity).
  So every system with it is consistent (part 1, with $p = m$)
  and has exactly one solution (part 2, with $p = n$),
  namely $\matr{A}^{-1} \vecf{b}$, since $\matr{A}\,(\matr{A}^{-1} \vecf{b}) = \vecf{b}$.

:::
